sentences.text:
The petitioner vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seeks quashing of Fir No.309/2020 dated 29.06.2020 registered under Sections 498A/406 of
the Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered at Ps.: Patel Nagar, Delhi and all proceeding emanating
therefrom, in view of the fact that the parties have settled all their disputes amicably and are now
living together.

2.  This petition is supported by affidavits of the petitioner and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 6728/2023 page 1 of 3
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2023 at 23:18:39 3.
Petitioner and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the Investigating Officer.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the said FIR.

sentences.text: Respondent no.2 confirms that she has voluntarily settled all her disputes with the petitioner, of her own accord without any duress, coercion or pressure.
She further states that she does not wish to pursue the criminal proceedings against the petitioner and has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the fact that the disputes arise out of matrimonial discord and settlement has been arrived at between the parties, and as the respondent no.2 does not wish to continue with the criminal proceedings, in order to bring a quietus to the present disputes, and for the well-being of the children and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab &
Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

sentences.text: 8. The parties herein i.e. the petitioner and the respondent no.2 being Dentists by profession, on their own free will, as a gesture of goodwill, have agreed to voluntarily provide their services by CRL.M.C. 6728/2023 page 2 of 3
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2023 at 23:18:39 conducting free basic dental check-ups for all the Delhi Police personnel stationed at the PS.: Patel Nagar, Delhi on the next three Sundays i.e. 24.09.2023, 01.10.2023 and 08.10.2023 between 11:00 AM till 01:00PM.
9. This Court highly appreciates the efforts of the parties for rendering their services towards the welfare of the Police personnel.

10. Therefore, the petition is allowed and FIR No.309/2020 dated 29.06.2020 registered under Sections 498A/406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 registered at PS.: Patel Nagar, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom are quashed.

11. Accordingly, the present petition alongwith the pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.
 
 SEPTEMBER 18, 2023/So  CRL.M.C. 6728/2023  This is a digitally signed order.
